cases.blind_review_reason: Four declared outcomes each get a Welch t-test judged at an unadjusted 0.05 threshold, with body mass (p = 0.0104) called significant. No family-wise control of any kind is applied.

Six declared outcomes each get a Welch t-test judged at an unadjusted 0.05 threshold, with four called significant. The report states each outcome is judged on its own at p < 0.05 and no correction is applied anywhere.

Three declared outcomes are each tested with a two-sample t-test and declared significant at a raw p < 0.05, with no correction anywhere in the script or report. All three are called significant on unadjusted p-values of 0.0133, 0.0303 and 0.0341.

Eight declared outcomes each get a Welch t-test judged at an unadjusted 0.05 threshold, with five called significant, including borderline calls that depend on the missing correction. No family-wise control appears in the script or report.

Only the two primary outcomes are Holm-adjusted; the remaining five members of the same declared family of seven are judged on raw p-values at 0.05, and three of them are called significant (p = 0.000049, 0.0049, 0.000305). Part of the family is controlled and the rest is not.

Bonferroni is applied by hand to only three of the five declared outcomes (multiplied by 3, not 5), while stool consistency and quality of life are judged on raw p-values, with quality of life called significant at raw p = 0.0418. Part of the family is corrected and part is not.

All five raw p-values are passed together in one multipletests call, whose default method (Holm-Sidak) controls the family-wise error rate, and every verdict is read from the adjusted values. The adjusted p-values in the report match Holm-Sidak on a family of five.
A Sidak per-comparison threshold computed from the full declared family size of four (0.012741 for family-wise 0.05) is applied to all four outcome verdicts, not the conventional 0.05.

All five raw p-values are adjusted together as one family with the Holm step-down method via pingouin.multicomp at family-wise alpha 0.05, and every verdict comes from the adjusted values. Two outcomes under a raw 0.05 are correctly reported as not significant.

All five declared outcomes are adjusted together with a correctly implemented hand-coded Holm step-down procedure at family-wise 0.05, and every verdict is read from the adjusted p-values. The single sensitivity re-run is explicitly descriptive and carries no verdict.

Discovery/validation split: all six outcomes are screened in the discovery half, and the only conclusions come from the validation half at a Bonferroni-adjusted level (0.05 / 5 carried forward = 0.01). Screening results are explicitly not reported as findings.

A single global screening statistic gates the analysis, but once it passes all five outcomes get unadjusted Welch t-tests at 0.05, with two called significant (p = 0.0036 and p = 0.0490). An omnibus gate followed by unadjusted per-outcome tests does not control the family-wise error in the strong sense, and the report itself states no adjustment is applied.

All testing and the Holm-Bonferroni adjustment across the whole family of five were done upstream; this project uses the released family-adjusted p-values as they are for every one of the five verdicts and computes nothing on the raw data beyond descriptive summaries.

All six declared outcomes are judged against a permutation max-statistic reference distribution (5000 label shuffles, 95th percentile of the family maximum), and the reported adjusted p-values come from that same family-maximum distribution. No verdict uses an unadjusted per-outcome p-value.

The protocol pre-specified a per-outcome threshold of 0.01, which is exactly Bonferroni over the declared family of five at a family-wise 0.05, and every one of the five verdicts is taken at that threshold. Two outcomes below 0.05 are correctly reported as not significant.
